title: Creating Pull Requests
learning_objectives: Understand what pull requests are and why they're essential for code review
Push feature branches to GitHub remote repository
Open a pull request through GitHub web interface
Write clear PR titles and descriptions using best practices
Link PRs to GitHub issues for traceability
Understand PR status checks and continuous integration basics
Apply PR workflow to CatchBook feature development
outline: Introduction: Pull requests as collaboration and quality gates
What is a pull request? Proposing changes for review before merge
The GitHub Flow: branch → commit → push → PR → review → merge
Opening a PR on GitHub: web interface walkthrough
Writing effective PR descriptions: what, why, how, testing
PR title conventions: aligning with Conventional Commits
Understanding PR diff view: changed files, line-by-line comparison
Hands-on: Push feature/update-readme and open CatchBook PR
Status checks preview: CI/CD integration (detailed in Phase 21)

catchbook_context.feature: Pull request workflow for CatchBook feature integration
catchbook_context.deliverable: Open PR to merge feature/update-readme into main with professional description

criteria: Push feature branch to GitHub successfully
Open PR with clear title following Conventional Commits format
Write PR description with context, changes, and testing notes
Link PR to a GitHub issue (create issue if needed)
Verify PR diff shows expected changes only
Explain why PRs improve CatchBook code quality and team collaboration

resources.title: How to Write the Perfect Pull Request
